==English==
{{wp}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|jewelry||US}}

===Etymology===
{{inh+|en|enm|juelrye}}, from {{der|en|fro|juelerye}}, equivalent to {{af|en|jewel|-ery}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈd͡ʒuː(ə)lɹi/|/ˈd͡ʒʊ-/|a2=US,also|ref2=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/jewelry}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-jewellery.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈd͡ʒuː(ə)ləɹi/|a=nonstandard|qq=this pronunciation gives rise to the Cockney rhyming slang ''{{l|en|tomfoolery}}''}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Aadenboy-jewellery.wav|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/dʒʋɛl(lə)ri/|a=Indic}}
* {{hyph|en|jew'el|lery}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|+}}

# Collectively, [[personal]] [[ornamentation]] such as [[ring]]s, [[necklace]]s, [[brooch]]es and [[bracelet]]s, made of [[precious]] [[metal]]s and sometimes [[set]] with [[gemstone]]s.
#: {{syn|en|bling|bling-bling|tom|q3=[[Cockney rhyming slang]]|tomfoolery|q4=Cockney rhyming slang}}
#: {{ux|en| The '''jewellery''' was very expensive in that shop.}}
#: {{ux|en|She had more '''jewellery''' ornamented about her than any three ladies needed.}}
#* {{RQ:Orczy Miss Elliott|chapter=The Fate of the ''Artemis''|passage=“{{...}} Captain Markam had been found lying half-insensible, gagged and bound, on the floor of the sitting-room, his hands and feet tightly pinioned, and a woollen comforter wound closely round his mouth and neck ; whilst Mrs. Markham's jewel-case, containing valuable '''jewellery''' and the secret plans of Port Arthur, had disappeared.{{nb...}}”}}
# {{lb|en|oil drilling|informal}} Any tools, instruments, devices, etc., placed within a [[drill pipe]].
# The shop from which a jeweller trades or makes jewellery

====Synonyms====
* see also [[Thesaurus:jewelry]]
